robotics-controls-25-se2-composition-ord.essentialQuestion: Why can two coordinate transforms have the same combined yaw but different world positions?
robotics-controls-25-se2-composition-ord.verifiedBoundary: SE(2) transform composition requires rotating the downstream translation: (Ra,ta)∘(Rb,tb)=(RaRb,Ra tb+ta); swapping terms generally changes position.
robotics-controls-25-se2-composition-ord.analogy: Engineering interpretation: why can two coordinate transforms have the same combined yaw but different world positions

starter.helper: Reverse A and B and assert (2.066025404,1.332050808,pi/3), rejecting the additive-only shortcut.

technical.scope: Synthetic, offline educational case. Stationary planar world/base/sensor frames; meters, positive counterclockwise yaw; no uncertainty or motion. Reference: https://github.com/ros2/ros2_documentation/blob/rolling/source/ROS-Framework/client-libraries/Working-with-Client-Libraries/Tf2/Time-Travel-With-Tf2-Cpp.rst

Rotate sensor translation by +90°: (0.2,0.1)→(-0.1,+0.2) m, then add (1,2): world sensor position (0.9,2.2) m.
Yaw adds to +60°; independent direct transformation of sensor origin (0,0) through base and then world also yields (0.9,2.2) m.
In reversed composition, rotate (1,2) m by -30° and add (0.2,0.1) m: position becomes (2.066025404,1.332050808) m, not (0.9,2.2) m.
Counterexample: raw addition of translations (1.2,2.1) m ignores the rotation and predicts neither composition correctly.

Two pure planar rotations about the same origin commute, but full translated poses generally do not; keep source/target frame labels ordered. robotics-controls-26-timestamp-pose-skew.essentialQuestion: How large is the artificial position discrepancy when sensor poses have different acquisition times?
robotics-controls-26-timestamp-pose-skew.verifiedBoundary: At constant signed speed v, samples separated by Δt differ by vΔt; alignment by linear interpolation is exact only for constant-velocity motion over that interval.
robotics-controls-26-timestamp-pose-skew.analogy: Engineering interpretation: how large is the artificial position discrepancy when sensor poses have different acquisition times

starter.helper: Assert unaligned endpoint mismatch 0.05 m; verify reversed speed gives -0.05 m.

technical.scope: Synthetic, offline educational case. Synthetic one-dimensional constant-speed pose, common clock in seconds; acceleration counterexample separate. At common time t=4.05 s, interpolation between endpoints gives 0.025 m; evaluating the constant-speed equation independently gives 0.025 m.
Reversing speed to -0.50 m/s reverses the apparent difference to -0.050 m; an unsigned timestamp delta alone loses this direction.
Counterexample: accelerated displacement p(t)=t² m over [0,0.10] s gives true midpoint p(0.05)=0.0025 m while midpoint interpolation predicts 0.005 m.

Timed transforms can align timestamped observations under suitable models; they cannot infer unspecified acceleration or clock skew. Source: https://github.com/ros2/ros2_documentation/blob/rolling/source/ROS-Framework/client-libraries/Working-with-Client-Libraries/Tf2/Time-Travel-With-Tf2-Cpp.rst

robotics-controls-27-encoder-modulo-roll.essentialQuestion: Why does a wrapped encoder reading not necessarily mean the wheel turned backward?
robotics-controls-27-encoder-modulo-roll.verifiedBoundary: For modulus M, shortest signed count change is wrap(c1-c0) to [-M/2,M/2); it is unique only when actual sample-to-sample travel is strictly less than M/2 counts.
robotics-controls-27-encoder-modulo-roll.analogy: Engineering interpretation: why does a wrapped encoder reading not necessarily mean the wheel turned backward

robotics-controls-28-effective-track-cal.verifiedBoundary: Under ideal no-slip differential-drive motion, b=(dR-dL)/Δθ for nonzero yaw change; small denominators make single-sample estimates sensitive to error.
robotics-controls-28-effective-track-cal.analogy: Engineering interpretation: how does an independent yaw reference constrain differential-drive track width

robotics-controls-29-angular-innovation-.essentialQuestion: How do prediction and measurement variances change a synthetic heading gate?
robotics-controls-29-angular-innovation-.verifiedBoundary: For independent heading errors, S=P+R and normalized angular innovation is |wrap(z-x)|/sqrt(S); a chosen 2-sigma gate is evidence of inconsistency, not a diagnosis.
robotics-controls-29-angular-innovation-.analogy: Engineering interpretation: how do prediction and measurement variances change a synthetic heading gate

Wrap periodic heading differences before gating. Rejection is statistical model evidence, not proof of a broken gyro or physical safety risk. Source: https://docs.wpilib.org/en/latest/docs/software/kinematics-and-odometry/differential-drive-odometry.html

robotics-controls-30-delay-aware-stoppin.essentialQuestion: Why can a control delay invalidate a braking-distance-only robot plan?
robotics-controls-30-delay-aware-stoppin.verifiedBoundary: Under ideal constant speed during delay τ followed by constant deceleration a>0, total modeled stop travel is vτ+v²/(2a); it is not a safety-certified physical stop distance.
robotics-controls-30-delay-aware-stoppin.analogy: Engineering interpretation: why can a control delay invalidate a braking-distance-only robot plan

technical.scope: Synthetic, offline educational case. Synthetic 1D stop scenario v=1.00 m/s, τ=0.10 s, a=2.00 m/s²; no real actuation. Reference: https://docs.wpilib.org/en/stable/docs/software/advanced-controls/controllers/trapezoidal-profiles.html
technical.versionCaution: This mathematical case supplies no real-robot operational authorization or safety certification; source material supports background concepts, not verification of the invented synthetic measurements.

Braking duration is v/a=0.50 s; subsequent braking travel v²/(2a)=0.25 m, totaling 0.35 m in 0.60 s.

robotics-controls-31-encoder-clock-jitte.essentialQuestion: How does measurement timestamp jitter corrupt a finite-difference wheel speed?
robotics-controls-31-encoder-clock-jitte.verifiedBoundary: Average wheel speed Δs/Δt must use the actual positive acquisition interval; nominal controller periods can bias the estimate without any count error.
robotics-controls-31-encoder-clock-jitte.analogy: Engineering interpretation: how does measurement timestamp jitter corrupt a finite-difference wheel speed

technical.scope: Synthetic, offline educational case. Synthetic displacement 0.020 m, timestamps 1.000 and 1.080 s, nominal period 0.100 s; no wheel slip. Reference: https://docs.wpilib.org/en/latest/docs/software/kinematics-and-odometry/differential-drive-odometry.html

robotics-controls-32-pi-backcalculation.essentialQuestion: How does saturation feedback change a discrete PI integrator without freezing it entirely?
robotics-controls-32-pi-backcalculation.verifiedBoundary: Specified back-calculation update I_next=I+Ki e dt+Kaw(u_sat-u_raw)dt corrects the integrator toward the clipped command; its sign matters.
robotics-controls-32-pi-backcalculation.analogy: Engineering interpretation: how does saturation feedback change a discrete pi integrator without freezing it entirely

technical.scope: Synthetic, offline educational case. Synthetic normalized command limit ±1, Kp=2, Ki=1/s, Kaw=2/s, I=0.5, e=+1, dt=.1s; no real plant. Reference: https://docs.wpilib.org/en/latest/docs/software/advanced-controls/controllers/pidcontroller.html
technical.versionCaution: This mathematical case supplies no real-robot operational authorization or safety certification; source material supports background concepts, not verification of the invented synthetic measurements.

Negative symmetric case I=-0.5,e=-1 produces u_raw=-2.5,u_sat=-1 and I_next=-0.3; no physical control tuning is established. Source: https://docs.wpilib.org/en/latest/docs/software/advanced-controls/controllers/pidcontroller.html

robotics-controls-35-shortest-heading-in.essentialQuestion: How should a robot interpolate yaw across the -180°/+180° representation boundary?
robotics-controls-35-shortest-heading-in.verifiedBoundary: Shortest-arc yaw interpolation is wrap(θ0+f wrap(θ1-θ0)); exactly 180° separation leaves a tie between two equally short directions.
robotics-controls-35-shortest-heading-in.analogy: Engineering interpretation: how should a robot interpolate yaw across the -180°/+180° representation boundary

technical.scope: Synthetic, offline educational case. Synthetic planar heading in degrees; f in [0,1], fixed angular rate along the chosen shortest arc. Reference: https://github.com/ros2/ros2_documentation/blob/rolling/source/ROS-Framework/client-libraries/Working-with-Client-Libraries/Tf2/Time-Travel-With-Tf2-Cpp.rst
technical.versionCaution: This mathematical case supplies no real-robot operational authorization or safety certification; source material supports background concepts, not verification of the invented synthetic measurements.

reasoningSteps: Use θ0=+170° at t=0 s and θ1=-170° at t=1 s; raw arithmetic delta is -340°.
Wrapped shortest signed delta is +20°, so at f=0.25 the heading is wrap(170+5)=+175°.
At f=0.75 the unwrapped angle is 170+15=185°, equivalent to -175° under [-180°,180°) normalization.
Independent relative-angle check gives +5° and +15° quarter and three-quarter progress, consistent with +20° total rotation.
Counterexample: naive signed-number interpolation gives +85° at f=0.25, implying an unnecessary -85° movement.

At exact 180° endpoint separation both rotation directions are equally short; a convention or additional data is required. Source: https://github.com/ros2/ros2_documentation/blob/rolling/source/ROS-Framework/client-libraries/Working-with-Client-Libraries/Tf2/Time-Travel-With-Tf2-Cpp.rst

technical.scope: Synthetic, offline educational case. Synthetic obstacle half-plane x≥1.0 m; radius 0.20 m; hard bounded center uncertainty ±0.15 m; static geometry only. Reference: https://docs.wpilib.org/en/latest/docs/software/kinematics-and-odometry/differential-drive-odometry.html
technical.versionCaution: This mathematical case supplies no real-robot operational authorization or safety certification; source material supports background concepts, not verification of the invented synthetic measurements.

reasoningSteps: Let obstacle begin at x=1.00 m, estimated center xhat=0.70 m, circular-footprint radius r=0.20 m and guaranteed location error |x-xhat|≤0.15 m.
Maximum possible right edge is 0.70+0.15+0.20=1.05 m, overlapping obstacle by 0.05 m.
At estimate xhat=0.60 m, worst right edge is 0.60+0.15+0.20=0.95 m, yielding 0.05 m positive geometric separation.
Independent interval construction gives possible centers [0.55,0.85] m at xhat=0.70; adding radius to upper endpoint returns x=1.05 m.
Counterexample: checking only xhat+r=0.90 m suggests 0.10 m free space, while a permitted actual location produces collision.

A 3σ interval is probabilistic, not a hard limit absent a validated confidence model; static clearance also omits stopping distance and control latency. Source: https://docs.wpilib.org/en/latest/docs/software/kinematics-and-odometry/differential-drive-odometry.html
